newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean unions to strike at Hyundai, dockyards.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean unions to strike at Hyundai, dockyards.

text.p: Union workers at Hyundai Group, South Korea's largest industrial conglomerate, will begin an indefinite strike at 1.00 p.m. (0400 GMT) on Thursday in protest at a new labour law, a union official said.

At the same time, workers at six leading shipyards will strike, their union body said. The shipyards are Hyundai Heavy Industries, Hyundai Mipo Dockyards, Daewoo Heavy Industries, Halla Heavy Industries, Hanjin Heavy Industries and Korea Tacoma.

Unions at Hyundai Group and the dockyards are affiliated with the outlawed Korea Confederation of Trade Unions that instructed all its 500,000 members to walk out shortly after passage of the labour law on Thursday.
South Korea's other main shipyard is operated by the Samsung Group. Samsung workers are not unionised.
The stoppage at Hyundai would also affect Hyundai Motor, South Korea's largest carmaker.
